bands.heading: Where most rental math goes wrong
body: The two errors that account for most bad purchases are a rent figure pulled from a national estimator rather than from what is actually leasing nearby, and a carrying cost that stops at principal and interest.

Taxes, insurance, vacancy, and maintenance are not rounding. Leave them out and a property that loses money every month can look like it clears a few hundred. Alex runs all of them, and he would rather talk you out of a bad address than sell you one.

bands.heading: Run it with the whole carry, not just the payment
body: Vacancy and maintenance are fields here rather than footnotes, because leaving them out is what turns a property that loses money every month into one that looks like it clears a few hundred.
If the number at the bottom is negative, it says so in the same size type as everything else.

bands.line: Already have an address? Skip the tool and send it to Alex.

bands.heading: What you get back on a specific address

steps.title: Rent, from comparable leases
steps.detail: What similar properties nearby are actually renting for right now, not a percentage applied to the purchase price.

steps.title: The full monthly carry
steps.detail: Debt service, taxes, insurance, and a maintenance allowance, with the assumption behind each number written down so you can argue with it.

steps.title: What is left
steps.detail: The number at the bottom, before and after vacancy. If it is negative, it says so in the same size type as everything else.

steps.title: What it needs before a tenant
steps.detail: The work required to make it rentable and roughly what that runs, because a purchase price plus fifteen thousand dollars of deferred maintenance is a different deal.

steps.title: Alex's read
steps.detail: Whether he would buy it, and why. This is the part that is worth asking for, and it is the part he will not soften.

items.q: Will you tell me a deal is bad?
items.a: Yes, and that is most of the value. An agent who approves every address you send is not screening anything, they are processing paperwork.

items.q: Do you work with people buying their first rental?
items.a: Yes. The analysis is the same either way, and the first one is where an honest second opinion is worth the most.

items.q: Can you look at more than one address at a time?
items.a: Send them together. Comparing several properties side by side is more useful than looking at one in isolation, and it is faster to work them as a batch.

items.q: What about properties that need significant work?
items.a: Those need a scope and a contractor number before the analysis means anything. Alex will tell you when a property cannot be evaluated responsibly without one rather than guessing at a rehab figure.
